info.title: CSC - Catalog of Second Chances - Backend API
info.description: Backend API for Catalog of Second Chances. FastAPI + MongoDB (async).

post.summary: Login (email or username) -> JWT
Register (open domains, or with an invitation code)

get.description: Verify user's email address using the token sent via email.

post.summary: Change password for the authenticated user
post.description:
Allows an authenticated user to change their own password.
Requires the correct current password and a new password (min 8 chars).

post.summary: Resend verification email (always the same answer)
post.description:
Always the same answer: no account is revealed. For an unverified account
a new token is stored (as a hash) and mailed in a background task; at
most ``VERIFICATION_MAILS_PER_HOUR`` mails go to one address in an hour
(the limiter counts the requests per client address).

post.summary: Ask for a password reset mail (always 202)
post.description:
Always 202 with the same text: no account is revealed. For an enabled
account a single-use token is stored (as a hash, one hour) and mailed;
at most ``RESET_MAILS_PER_HOUR`` mails go to one address in an hour (the
limiter counts the requests per client address).

post.summary: Choose a new password with the mailed token
post.description:
The token works once and for an hour. It sets the password, signs out
every token issued before (``password_changed_at``) and, because the mail
reached the mailbox, counts as the verification of the address.

get.description: The product version and its release tag; used by the deploy health check.
The Grasshopper interface release that belongs to this backend.

The components of the release (a signed-in caller may name a ``?channel=``
branch or tag; an anonymous caller always gets the release): name,
nickname, subcategory, description, inputs from the ``RunScript``
signature with the descriptions ``BeforeRunScript`` sets, outputs from
``OUTPUTS`` (decision 8.112). The sources are only parsed (``ast``), never
run; one that does not parse is listed under ``skipped`` with a note. A
parse is kept per blob sha, so a release costs one directory listing and
the sources it has not read yet.
Download this backend's Grasshopper interface release as a ZIP.

patch.description:
``moderator(D)``; while unpublished also its creator (8.9). Patching a
field of an inherited unit makes the unit the component's own; adding
a unit to ``inherited_fields`` takes it back from the parents. A
changed unit propagates to every descendant still inheriting it
(8.31). ``material`` without ``material_class`` re-derives the class;
``material_class: null`` returns it to derived (I25).

delete.description:
Without ``purge``: only while nothing of it was ever published (I19),
by its creator or moderator(D); snapshots and files go with it.
``?purge=1`` (admin; the body repeats the id and gives a reason):
anything, evidence included, leaving 410 stubs for every id.

post.summary: Take a component out of circulation (moderator(D))
post.description:
Installed, recycled, disposed, returned, lost --- or a hand-set
``split`` without catalogued pieces. ``merged`` is only ever set by the
server (8.8). ``construction_work`` only for ``installed`` (I18).

delete.description:
Not for a split / merge the server keeps from published children:
withdraw the child instead (8.8).

post.summary: Bring a component back into circulation (moderator(D))
post.description:
An installed, returned or lost piece comes back with a new origin; the
old ``{origin, exit}`` goes to ``past_cycles`` (3.1.3). Terminal exits
cannot re-enter (I18). The next snapshot defaults to the new
``origin.at`` (8.19). A re-entered child owns its new origin.

post.summary: Record the deinstallation of an in-place piece (moderator(D))
post.description:
``planned`` becomes false and the given fields go into the existing
origin; ``kind`` may switch to ``demolition``. A reservation survives;
no snapshot is created. The origin is now the piece's own, and every
descendant that still inherits it follows, like a parent's PATCH of
``origin`` (3.1.2, 8.110).

post.summary: Take a deinstallation back, while nothing follows it (moderator(D))
post.description:
``planned`` is true again, but only while no state starts and no
evidence is valid after the deinstallation's ``at``; later than that a
moderator corrects the origin by PATCH (8.104). Propagates like the
deinstall.

get.summary: Change log of a component (members of D, admin)
get.description:
Entries of the identity, its snapshots and evidence, newest first.
Old values may name people, so the log is for members only (8.36).

post.summary: Add a material (admin)

patch.description:
``_id`` is immutable (a rename is a merge into a new id). A new
``default_class`` re-derives every derived ``material_class`` (I25).

delete.description: Only while no identity references it, withdrawn ones included.

post.summary: Merge a material into another (admin)
post.description:
Every identity moves to the target; derived classes follow the
target's default, assigned ones stay; ``mid`` remains as an alias
``{_id, merged_into}`` so old references resolve (8.35).

patch.summary: Edit a record; per-field permission (8.3, I13)
patch.description:
A draft: author or ``moderator(D)``; a pending record: ``moderator(D)``
(8.18); a rejected one: nobody. Before publish any field of the create
body may change --- ``payload`` and ``performed_by`` are replaced as a
whole, ``position`` is merged; resend a stored payload without its
server-computed fields --- and the record is recomputed and checked
again; a result change resets ``reviewed`` / ``accredited`` to
``unverified`` (8.12). After publish only ``notes`` and
``position.description`` change, by ``moderator(D)``; frozen fields
--> 409 pointing at ``/supersede`` (I13), server-maintained fields
--> 422.

delete.description:
Only draft / pending / rejected (I15); a published one is withdrawn
instead. Its files go with it. Refused while a core names it as its
pair.

get.description:
The snapshot block (the materialized as-of fold): the snapshot-scoped
quantities whose records resolve to this state.

get.summary: What happened to a component, merged
get.description:
Archived cycles, the origin, every state and correction, every
evidence record (where it falls: before cataloguing, in the history,
after the piece left circulation), changes of the metadata and the exit.
What the caller may not see is left out; a withdrawn record outside the
dataset is a bare row; outside the dataset a metadata change shows only
its date (8.36).

post.summary: Attach one upload to several evidence records
post.description:
Before publish as any edit of the record (7.0: a draft --- author or
``moderator(D)``; a pending record --- ``moderator(D)``); after publish
``contributor(D)`` adds (add-only, I24). The permission is checked for
every record before anything is stored. The same document twice on one
record is refused (409).

get.description:
The list as the viewer may see it. Anonymous readers of a public
piece get media type, size, checksum and date --- no names, no
uploaders --- and "sign in to download" (8.13).

Signed-in users who can see the record, whatever the component's
visibility; anonymous callers get 401 (8.13). The files of a withdrawn
record are for members only (8.17).

delete.description:
Before publish: author / ``moderator(D)`` as any edit, the reason is
optional. After publish: ``moderator(D)`` with a reason. Either way the
file is deleted and the entry stays with ``removed {at, by_user_id,
reason}`` --- an index is never reused (I24). The reason ``gdpr`` blanks
the name, also in the change log; the checksum stays (decision 8.13).

post.summary: draft --> pending (author; never publishes, 8.120)
post.description:
Nobody publishes directly (8.120): for every role the submit only moves
draft --> pending; ``/publish`` (moderator(D)) is the separate step. The
old ``?publish=1`` of earlier clients is ignored.

post.summary: pending --> draft (author, 8.18)
rejected --> draft (author)
pending --> published (moderator(D))
pending --> rejected with a reason (moderator(D))
published --> withdrawn with a reason (moderator(D))
post.description:
Out of the fold and the public tier; members keep the full record
(8.17). Withdrawing a correction gives the record it corrected back its
place (it stays superseded only while its correction is live).

post.summary: withdrawn --> published (moderator(D))
Correct a published record (a new pending record)
post.description:
contributor(D). The body is the whole new record, of the same
method; it enters as ``pending``. On publish the old record is marked
superseded and leaves the fold and the default lists (3.3.4). 409 if a
correction of it is already open (I14, 8.16).

put.description:
The recorder toggles ``unverified`` <--> ``self_attested`` (when they
are among the performers, and never over a reviewer's state);
``reviewed`` / ``accredited`` and stepping a state back to
``unverified`` are for ``reviewer(D)`` or admin who is neither the
recorder nor a performer --- no admin exception (8.12, I27); a reviewer
never sets ``self_attested``. The server sets ``by`` and ``at``;
``accredited`` needs a note and an accreditation covering the standard
(I22). Changing the state of a published record recomputes the fold.

post.summary: Redact a person (admin, GDPR Art 17)
post.description:
Admin. The person is named by ``user_id`` or by ``name`` (+
``organization``). **A name without an organization blanks every actor
of that name catalogue-wide**: use ``dry_run`` to see what it would
touch. Writes are guarded by the record's etag (identity:
``lastmodified``) and retried; a record that keeps changing is a 409
and the run can be repeated. Returns what was changed and the worklist
of attachments to replace by redacted copies.

get.summary: Lanes and events of a component and its relatives
get.description:
The piece is the middle lane (level 0), parents have negative levels
and children positive ones. Every lane has ``id``, ``role``, ``level``
and ``visible``; a visible one also its header and ``events``. ``links``
join a parent and a child lane (``cut``: one parent; ``assemble``:
several) at the child's first version. ``more`` counts the lanes left
out beyond twelve.

post.description:
Nobody publishes directly (8.120): for every role the submit only moves
draft --> pending. Publishing is the separate ``/publish`` route
(moderator(D)), also for a moderator's own submission. The old
``?publish=1&promote=1`` of earlier clients is not a parameter any more
and is ignored, so such a client still gets its plain submit.

patch.description:
Before publish: a draft --- author / moderator(D); a pending one ---
moderator(D) (8.18); a rejected one --- nobody. After publish:
moderator(D) for mutable metadata, valid time and overrides, and for a
frozen ``capture`` field that is still empty, once (8.123 a); other

withdrawn instead. Files go with it. ``?purge=1``: admin, anything,
leaves a 410 stub.

Return a single snapshot document. ETag == stored `etag` field.
A withdrawn one outside its dataset answers with its tombstone (8.17).

post.summary: Recompute every derived field of one snapshot (moderator(D))
post.description:
Runs all stages of the geometry runner (spec section 4.3) on the
snapshot, stale or not: frame, shape class (unless assigned), proxies
and deviation maps, descriptors, complexity (unless assigned) and the
preview. Overrides stay. Works while the snapshot is a draft too.

post.summary: Withdraw a published component (moderator(D))
post.description:
Hidden everywhere by default; members of D see it in full, everyone
else who could see it a tombstone (8.17). With ``duplicate_of`` the
resolver and the component page lead to the canonical piece; pieces
that named this one as their canonical piece follow along (I19).

post.summary: Reinstate a withdrawn component (moderator(D))

get.description:
``Accept: text/html`` --> 302 to the component page; otherwise 302 to
the passport. A withdrawn duplicate --> 301 to ``/id/{duplicate_of}``;
other withdrawn pieces and pieces without a current state still
redirect (the page shows the tombstone / "no current state"); purged
--> 410; unknown or never published (unless the caller may see it)
--> 404. Visibility applies after the redirect (8.11).

at request time (no duplicate files).

Returns 404 when the file is not on disk or ``mesh_ply_resolutions``
does not list the requested resolution for this primitive index.

put.summary: Upload or replace mesh PLY for snapshot primitive
put.description:
Store ``meshes/<snapshot_id>/<primitive_index>/{reduced|detailed}.ply``
and register the resolution on ``mesh_ply_resolutions``.

delete.summary: Delete mesh PLY for snapshot primitive
delete.description:
Remove ``meshes/<snapshot_id>/<primitive_index>/{reduced|detailed}.ply``
and drop the resolution from ``mesh_ply_resolutions`` when listed.

get.summary: Capture fixture mesh (e.g. the robot gripper; decision 7.7)
get.description:
Serve ``capture.fixtures[index].file`` (``capture/<snapshot_id>/
fixtures/<i>.ply`` under ``SNAPSHOT_CAPTURE_DIR``). Fixtures are capture
context, never the component: no derivation reads them.

get.summary: Export a proxy as a mesh (PLY or OBJ), in stored coordinates
get.description:
Triangulate ``geometry.proxies[index]`` (box, prism, cylinder or hull;
Appendix B) and place it with its ``placement``, so the mesh lies in the
snapshot's stored coordinates like the source geometry. OBJ is converted
on the fly.

get.summary: Deviation map of one proxy face (16-bit RGB PNG)
get.description:
Channels (spec appendix B): R = distance (``value * scale_mm +
offset_mm`` from ``deviation_maps.faces[face].distance``), G = normal
deviation (hundredths of a degree), B = occupancy. The face must be
listed in the proxy's ``deviation_maps``; nothing else is served.

get.summary: Get point cloud PLY (file on disk or generated from inline points)
get.description:
Serve ``point_clouds/<snapshot_id>/<index>.ply`` when present; otherwise
build PLY from ``geometry.point_clouds[index]`` inline points.

put.summary: Upload point cloud PLY for snapshot primitive
put.description:
Store ``point_clouds/<snapshot_id>/<index>.ply``.

``index`` must match an entry in ``geometry.point_clouds``.

delete.summary: Delete on-disk point cloud PLY for snapshot primitive

get.description: Serve snapshot_previews/{snapshot_id}.webp only.

get.summary: List occupied photo slot indices for a snapshot
get.description: Return sorted slot indices and count from disk (one directory read).

put.summary: Upload or replace user photo for snapshot
put.description: Accept up to upload limit; store JPEG scaled/compressed to max output.

delete.summary: Delete user photo slot for snapshot

get.summary: The caller, with the roles per dataset

patch.description:
``full_name``, ``organization``, ``organization_ror`` (a ROR id or
URL), ``orcid`` (format and check digit) and ``default_role``. Records
take the values over when they are written; a later change never rewrites
a record.

get.summary: Datasets the caller can see, with the caller's roles
get.description:
Admin: all. Signed in: member of, or ``catalog``. Anonymous: those
holding public components (3.6).

post.summary: Create a dataset (a verified account, or an admin)
post.description:
An account with a verified e-mail address creates a dataset of its own
(8.139): the slug is derived from the name, the creator becomes
``moderator`` and ``contributor``, the dataset is ``members`` and not
reviewed, and each account may create ``CSC_MAX_DATASETS_PER_USER`` of
them (3). An admin may state the slug, creates reviewed datasets and has
no limit. The admins get a "Dataset created" mail for an account's
dataset.

get.summary: One dataset; members for moderator(D) and admin

delete.description:
Only while the dataset holds no piece at all (no identity, whatever
its state; for an admin too: move the pieces first, ``move_identity``).
The open invitations into it are revoked with it (8.139 f).

put.summary: Set a member's roles; empty removes (moderator(D))

post.summary: Make every published piece of a dataset public or private (moderator(D))
post.description:
Sets ``is_public`` on the pieces of the dataset that were ever
published (3.1.5) and are not withdrawn, where the flag differs, and logs
each change like a metadata PATCH (``cause: patch``). Unpublished and
withdrawn pieces are left alone, and so are children: no piece follows
another (6.2). ``dry_run`` only counts.

get.summary: User accounts with memberships, filterable (admin only)
get.description:
Filters combine (8.21); memberships come from ``datasets.members``,
joined here in one pass.

parameters.name: dataset_role

schema.description: holds this role (in `dataset`, else in any)
schema.title: Dataset Role

parameters.description: holds this role (in `dataset`, else in any)

get.summary: Prefix search over username, name, email (admin; 8.20)

schema.title: Response Search Users Users Search Get

post.summary: Invite addresses (admin, or moderator(D) into D)
post.description:
One invitation per address. For an admin, and in a reviewed dataset, an
address that already has an account is reported (``exists``) --- add it
with the member editor. In a dataset an admin has not reviewed yet every
address is invited and the answer is the same for all: it does not tell
whether an address has an account (8.144 b).

get.summary: Invitations: admin all, moderators their datasets'

post.summary: Resend an invitation: a new code, the old one void
post.description:
Whoever may invite now may resend: the caller's current ``invite``
permission on the invitation's dataset (an admin for one without a
dataset), not the creation of the invitation --- a moderator who was
demoted cannot send it again (8.144 e). An open or an expired invitation
gets a new code (the old one stops working at once) and a new expiry (the
rule of a new invitation: ``expires_days`` from now, 14 by default), and
is mailed again; a used or revoked one is a 409. A resend counts for the
daily cap of mails.
The code is in no response: only the mailbox gets it (8.124 b).

post.summary: Add a person by email (moderator(D)); invites unknown addresses
post.description:
In a reviewed dataset (and for an admin): the exact address of an existing
account is added at once (roles are merged) and notified by mail; any
other address --- any domain --- gets an invitation into D with these
roles (8.20). In a dataset an admin has not reviewed yet every address
gets the invitation, with the same answer and the same mail, whether or
not it has an account: the account joins by opening the link signed in
with that address and accepting (8.144 b).

post.summary: What an invitation offers (the account it names)
post.description:
For the page ``/invite``: the dataset and the roles, only to the
signed-in account whose address the invitation names. The code goes in
the body, not in a URL (a URL is logged).

post.summary: Accept an invitation with an existing account
post.description:
The consent: the signed-in account whose address the invitation names
joins the dataset with the invited roles. An unknown code and another
address are the same 400. The invitation works once (the compare-and-set
of ``grant_invitation``).
